text:
The Flyers just swept a two-game road trip, finishing it with a 4-3 win in Montreal, and have won three straight. Enjoy it, but read the fine print: they outscored teams 14-11 in those games on 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and the extra came from 14 goals on 7.7 expected. Over the season they're at 46% of the expected goals and 44% at 5v5, and at 9-11-6 their record is almost exactly what their play deserves. Our playoff odds have them at 10%.

The best news is young. Matvei Michkov, Noah Cates and Porter Martone have won 62% of the expected goals together, the clearest bright spot on Rick Tocchet's lineup sheet. Denver Barkey has 8 points in his last 10 since coming back from injury (5.4 expected), and PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor is openly asking whether he's better than anyone thought.

The worries are the usual ones. Dan Vladar has a .850 save rate and is 4.1 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Trevor Zegras has 2 points in 10 games on 7.0 expected, a gap between chances and results rather than a lack of chances.

And the rumour mill is loud. RMNB reports the Flyers could approach Travis Konecny about waiving his no-movement clause, Konecny has downplayed the talk, and Michkov's name keeps showing up in trade pitches. For a team at 10%, what happens before the deadline may matter more than the next three weeks.
